city.name: Philosopher's Path
city.description: Kyoto's Philosopher's Path: a canal walk under the cherry trees from the Silver Pavilion to Nanzen-ji, past mossy temples, to the old brick aqueduct and the rails of the Keage Incline.

tour.title: The Philosopher's Path
tour.text: Two kilometres along a little canal at the foot of the eastern hills, from Ginkaku-ji to Nanzen-ji. In early April the cherries meet overhead; in November the maples burn red.

tour.title: Ginkaku-ji
tour.text: The Silver Pavilion, Ashikaga Yoshimasa's retreat of 1489, was never silvered. Its raked sand garden and moss are the purest Zen in Kyoto; the path begins at the bridge below.

tour.title: Along the canal
tour.text: The philosopher Nishida Kitaro walked here every day to think. Painter Hashimoto Kansetsu and his wife planted the cherries from 1922, and their petals still drift on the water each spring.

tour.title: Nanzen-ji and the aqueduct
tour.text: Climb the great Sanmon for the view a famous outlaw admired in kabuki: "Spectacular, spectacular!" Behind it, a red-brick Roman-style aqueduct carries the canal through the temple grounds.

tour.title: The Keage Incline
tour.text: Boats once rode cradles up and down these rails between the canal's two levels. Now it's a walk under the cherries, and on a spring weekend the most photographed tracks in Japan.

shore.encoding: r: 128 + 2 x signed distance to the shoreline (m, water positive); g: sand; b: rock

susuki.note: Susuki (trees.json susuki, #326): on the open grassland and meadows OpenStreetMap maps (natural=grassland, landuse=meadow: the unmown grass of the parks and the hills, where susuki is the grass that stands) (Overture base land, OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL; pipeline/grasses.py). Its heads stand from mid August to spring (web/trees.js).

trees.note: Species are not mapped; the mix is a guess from Kyoto's street-tree surveys and the temples' own guides. The Higashiyama hillsides above the path are a laurel forest with cedars, pines and maples. The path's own cherries (Kansetsu-zakura, first planted in 1922) are planted along both banks by city.py, every 4 to 5 m as photographs show them; the area round the path makes them and the mapped trees there cherries. The path is not lit at night, so no yozakura.

inland.note: Inland water at its own level, from pipeline/inland_water.py: rings [x, y, ...] local m (outer, then holes); bz the bank's height and wz the water's at each ring point (m); water_m the water's depth over the bed; decks: where a road crosses a walled channel without a bridge model, the ground kept over it.
